A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AtlasD and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original symmetry-discovery experiments and downstream results for top tagging, simulated heat flow, spherical MNIST, and ClimateNet, plus appendix experiments and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments on eight-element discrete symmetry recovery and PDE discovery with a sheared chart in Appendices D.5–D.6.

M1.justification: Local predictor training, Lie-algebra discovery, regularization, and normalized coset discovery and filtering are unchanged. Expanded Algorithm 1 spells out operations already described in v1; it does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds symmetry discovery for f(x,y)=|x|+|y|, extending the synthetic tasks to an eight-element D4 symmetry group. The original benchmark and arctan tasks remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the top-tagging, MNIST, ClimateNet, and PDE comparisons. LieGG's PDE comparison already appeared in v1 Appendix D.4; its increased prominence in v2 does not introduce a baseline.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1 and C.1 change the reported top-tagging coset initialization from K=256 to K=64, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. New Appendix D.5 uses K=256 and q=128, while D.6 evaluates a third PDE atlas containing a partially sheared chart.

E4.justification: New Appendices D.5–D.6 test recovery of a more complex discrete component group and robustness to chart distortion. Existing imperfect-symmetry, regularization, normalization, and LieGG analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run means and standard deviations for top tagging, select the best of ten ClimateNet runs, and retain the repeated-run arctan plot. The new experiments add no uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: Appendix D.5 newly reports recovery of all eight D4 elements. D.6 reports both cosets and the generator [[-0.368,-1.035],[1.101,0.386]] under chart shear. Tables 1–3, MNIST accuracies of 0.9381 versus 0.6975, and the retained discovery findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 defines sheaves and sheaf morphisms and argues that being a sheaf morphism is stronger than atlas locality. Section 4.2 adds the assumption that all members of symmetry orbits are represented in the data. The existing atlas definitions, theorems, proofs, and complexity analysis remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: formalizing atlas equivariance, discovering continuous and discrete local symmetries, and exploiting them in downstream gauge-equivariant networks. The additions support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly assumes that the trained predictor shares the dataset's symmetries and acknowledges that the MNIST atlas is idealized. It also discusses degraded discovery under chart shear, adding a specific qualification to robustness while retaining the original limitations.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a public-code statement and repository link absent from v1. Appendix D.5 supplies candidate and filtering counts for the new experiment, and C.1 revises the top-tagging count. The three-layer predictor newly described in the main text was already documented in v1 Appendix C.1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of approximate equivariance and conserved-quantity discovery, citing works such as Finzi et al., Wang et al., Veefkind and Cesa, Hou et al., and van der Ouderaa et al. Appendix A.1 adds Vakil for sheaf background. These extend context while retaining the central local-versus-global positioning.

P1.justification: v2 expands Algorithm 1 and the predictor explanation, makes localized wording corrections, and renames Appendix A and subsection D.1. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 splits the top-tagging heatmaps into Figures 4–5, enlarges and rearranges the PDE illustration, and moves v1 Figure 15's LieGG spectrum into the main text as Figure 8. It also adds Figures 17–18 for the new experiments. The tables retain their structure and contents.

improvement.justification: The new discrete-group and sheared-chart experiments provide targeted additional validation, while clearer pseudocode, explicit qualifications, and code-access information improve usability. The principal benchmark evidence remains unchanged, and the new tests are narrowly scoped without additional uncertainty reporting, so the overall improvement is limited.
